components.title: RideTube (fork by 7amoody1985)
components.description: TEST COPY of JustAnotherPU's RideTube 0.4.5 (github.com/JustAnotherPU/ridetube), not endorsed by its developer, under its own ids: it installs beside the original and never over it (one plays at a time). Its service streams the video in RAM instead of writing it to flash (the change offered to JustAnotherPU), and the setting 'Stream stats over the video' shows RAM, buffer, network and the picture's frame rate (freezes) while a video plays. Source: github.com/7amoody1985/ridetube, branch lab-ram
components.author: JustAnotherPU, modified by 7amoody1985

components.title: RideTube service (fork by 7amoody1985)
components.description: The service of the RideTube test copy (JustAnotherPU's 0.4.2, modified, with its own ids): yt-dlp fetches on the car, the sound through the BMW MediaPlayer, the picture decoded by ytdec. The playing video streams in RAM (a 256 MB tmpfs) instead of being written whole to flash; seeks, resumes and dropped links fetch from the fragment they need. Downloads keep one connection open. For CarLink's Car log: /run/mdq-ridetube-d/log.txt (its log, redacted, with 'LAB frames:' lines when the picture freezes while the sound plays on) and status.json. Needs Node.js 22 (jap-node22) from the JustAnotherPU/mgu-apps source. Source: github.com/7amoody1985/ridetube, branch lab-ram
components.author: JustAnotherPU, modified by 7amoody1985

components.title: CarLink (experimental)
components.description: Experimental. The next turn from HudHud or Google Maps on your phone, in the middle of the instrument cluster and as a home-screen widget, sent by the CarLink phone app. With the car on the phone's hotspot (the Store's Wi-Fi uplink), the car calls the phone; on the car's Wi-Fi or USB tethering, the phone calls the car. Demo shows it without the phone. Needs cluster-render from the robertnisipeanu/idrive-apps source.
components.author: 7amoody1985

components.title: Android Auto log (for CarLink)
components.description: Experimental. Copies the car's Android Auto daemon's log (journalctl -u aapd, the last 2000 lines) and a snapshot of its state, taken again when aapd starts or stops (systemctl status, waze-on-cluster's aapd patch, /etc/aapd.conf whole and against its backup, the network and its firewall, and what may keep Android Auto out of the iDrive menu: the boot journal's lines about Android Auto from every service, the coding and variant services and their files, by name, the head unit's coding as hex and the variant registries' strings about Android Auto / CarPlay / CarLife; any VIN redacted), every service's journal lines about Android Auto as they come (the car's journal keeps only about an hour), and since 0.1.4, once a start at the lowest priority, which program reads /etc/ConnVariants.cfg and the key names it holds, which programs mention Android Auto or its wireless Bluetooth service, and the process list, to /run/mdq-aapd-log, where CarLink shows it on the phone (Car log, Debug on). Runs as root but only reads; writes only that folder, which goes when it stops. Starts at the next head-unit start after its install.
components.author: 7amoody1985
